name: Italian Game
description: A practical 1.e4 course that teaches the Italian Game first, then shows what to do when Black avoids it.

branches.title: Main Line: Quiet Italian Setup
branches.description: Learn a sound beginner Italian Game setup: develop, castle, then prepare a central break.

moves.title: Claim the center
moves.explanation: Controls d5 and f5, opens lines for the bishop and queen, and starts the game with direct central space.

moves.title: Black mirrors the center
moves.explanation: Black also takes central space, creating an open game where quick development matters.

moves.title: Develop with a threat
moves.explanation: Nf3 develops a knight, attacks e5, and prepares castling without bringing the queen out too early.

moves.title: Black defends e5
moves.explanation: Nc6 develops while defending the e5 pawn. White should keep improving pieces instead of chasing pawns.

moves.title: Enter the Italian Game
moves.explanation: Bc4 develops to an active diagonal and points at f7, the most sensitive square near Black's king.

moves.title: Black chooses the classical setup
moves.explanation: Bc5 develops naturally and mirrors White's pressure. Both sides are racing to castle and finish development.

moves.title: Prepare d4
moves.explanation: c3 supports a later d4 break. This is the key Italian idea: build the center before opening it.

moves.title: Black develops and attacks e4
moves.explanation: Nf6 adds pressure to e4 and gets Black closer to castling.

moves.title: Support the center calmly
moves.explanation: d3 keeps e4 protected and opens the c1 bishop. Beginners can choose this quiet setup before learning sharper d4 lines.

moves.title: Black supports e5
moves.explanation: d6 protects e5 and opens the c8 bishop, keeping the position solid.

moves.title: Castle first
moves.explanation: White gets the king safe before starting central or kingside plans.

moves.title: Black castles too
moves.explanation: Both kings are safe. The opening is complete enough to start asking: which piece improves next?

moves.title: Put the rook on e1
moves.explanation: Re1 supports e4 and prepares the center break d4 under better conditions.

moves.title: Black asks the bishop a question later
moves.explanation: a6 prepares Ba7 and gives Black luft on the queenside without changing the main plan.

moves.title: Finish development
moves.explanation: Nbd2 connects pieces and supports f1, c4, and e4. White is ready for Nf1-g3 or d4 ideas.

moves.title: Black preserves the bishop
moves.explanation: Ba7 keeps pressure on f2 and avoids a future b4 tempo. The position is a normal Italian middlegame.

hints: Follow the highlighted move and say the idea out loud.
After each move, check king safety, center control, and piece activity.
When a trade appears, ask what file opens and which piece improves next.
coachingNotes: This is a real Italian Game: e4 e5, Nf3 Nc6, Bc4.
For beginners, the quiet plan is c3, d3, castle, Re1, then improve pieces before opening the center.
Only push d4 when your king is safe and your pieces are ready to handle trades.
Your middlegame plan is simple: safe king, active minor pieces, pressure on e5/f7, and one central break.

branches.title: If Black Plays c5: Simple Sicilian Response
branches.description: Black has avoided the Italian Game and entered the Sicilian. Use a calm open-center setup.

moves.title: Start with e4
moves.explanation: White takes central space and invites Black to show their defense.

moves.title: Black chooses the Sicilian
moves.explanation: c5 attacks d4 from the side. This is not an Italian Game, so switch plans calmly.

moves.title: Develop first
moves.explanation: Nf3 develops, controls d4/e5, and prepares the central break.

moves.title: Black supports the center
moves.explanation: d6 controls e5 and prepares Nf6, a very common Sicilian setup.

moves.title: Open the center
moves.explanation: d4 challenges Black immediately. This is the clean beginner way to avoid drifting with slow moves.

moves.title: Black trades in the center
moves.explanation: Black captures on d4, opening the c-file and changing the pawn structure.

moves.title: Recapture with the knight
moves.explanation: Nxd4 develops a piece into the center. After this trade, White has active pieces and clear development.

moves.title: Black attacks e4
moves.explanation: Nf6 develops and asks White to defend the e4 pawn.

moves.title: Defend e4 naturally
moves.explanation: Nc3 protects e4 and completes the central knight setup.

moves.title: Black prepares queenside play
moves.explanation: a6 is common in Sicilian structures. Do not panic; continue development and castle.

moves.title: Prepare to castle
moves.explanation: Be2 is a calm square that keeps the king safe and avoids unnecessary early attacks.

moves.title: Black prepares development
moves.explanation: e6 opens the f8 bishop and supports central control.

moves.title: Castle
moves.explanation: White gets safe before choosing a plan like Be3, Qd2, or f4 later.

moves.title: Black develops
moves.explanation: Be7 prepares castling. The opening has become a normal Sicilian middlegame, not an Italian attack.

hints: Follow the highlighted move and say the idea out loud.
After each move, check king safety, center control, and piece activity.
When a trade appears, ask what file opens and which piece improves next.
coachingNotes: Black avoided the Italian with 1...c5, so this branch is a Sicilian response, not an Italian continuation.
The beginner plan is Nf3, d4, recapture with the knight, develop, and castle.
Do not use Italian ideas like Bc4 pressure on f7 automatically here; the pawn structure is different.
After the opening, watch the d-file/c-file and keep your e4 pawn supported.

branches.title: If Black Plays c6: Caro-Kann Response
branches.description: Black prepares d5. Build the center and choose a clear Advance-style plan.

moves.title: Start with e4
moves.explanation: White controls the center and opens lines for the bishop and queen.

moves.title: Black chooses the Caro-Kann
moves.explanation: c6 prepares d5 with support. This is solid and not part of the Italian Game.

moves.title: Build the pawn center
moves.explanation: d4 creates a strong center before Black challenges it.

moves.title: Black challenges e4
moves.explanation: d5 is the Caro-Kann idea: attack the center with a supported pawn.

moves.title: Advance with space
moves.explanation: e5 gains space and creates a clear beginner plan: develop behind the pawn chain.

moves.title: Black develops the light bishop
moves.explanation: Bf5 gets the bishop outside the pawn chain before e6.

moves.title: Develop calmly
moves.explanation: Nf3 supports the center and prepares castling.

moves.title: Black supports d5
moves.explanation: e6 builds a solid pawn chain but locks in the dark-square bishop.

moves.title: Prepare castling
moves.explanation: Be2 is simple and safe. White should not start pawn storms before the king is secure.

moves.title: Black attacks the chain
moves.explanation: c5 is Black's main break against the advanced e5 pawn.

moves.title: Castle
moves.explanation: White castles before deciding whether to capture, support d4, or improve pieces.

moves.title: Black develops pressure
moves.explanation: Nc6 adds pressure to d4. The next lesson is to defend the center without freezing your pieces.

hints: Follow the highlighted move and say the idea out loud.
After each move, check king safety, center control, and piece activity.
When a trade appears, ask what file opens and which piece improves next.
coachingNotes: Black avoided the Italian with 1...c6, so this is a Caro-Kann response branch.
The Advance setup teaches space: e5 gives room, but you must support the pawn chain.
A common mistake is attacking too soon. Develop, castle, and only then consider kingside space gains.
Watch Black's c5 break; it is the main challenge to your center.

branches.title: If Black Plays e6: French Defense Response
branches.description: Black prepares d5. Take space, build a pawn chain, and develop around it.

moves.title: Start with e4
moves.explanation: White claims central space and opens piece lines.

moves.title: Black chooses the French
moves.explanation: e6 prepares d5 and creates a more closed center than the Italian.

moves.title: Build the center
moves.explanation: d4 takes the space Black is about to challenge.

moves.title: Black attacks e4
moves.explanation: d5 is the French Defense structure. Black challenges the center immediately.

moves.title: Advance for space
moves.explanation: e5 gains space and starts the classic French pawn chain.

moves.title: Black attacks d4
moves.explanation: c5 is Black's main counterplay against the pawn chain.

moves.title: Support the chain
moves.explanation: c3 protects d4. This is the simple beginner way to keep the center stable.

moves.title: Black adds pressure
moves.explanation: Nc6 attacks d4 again and develops.

moves.title: Develop and defend
moves.explanation: Nf3 supports d4 and prepares castling.

moves.title: Black pressures d4 and b2
moves.explanation: Qb6 is a common French idea. Notice how Black targets the base of your pawn chain.

moves.title: Develop actively
moves.explanation: Bd3 points toward h7 and helps White castle.

moves.title: Black trades at the base
moves.explanation: cxd4 challenges the support pawn. This is the kind of trade French players look for.

moves.title: Recapture and keep space
moves.explanation: cxd4 restores the pawn chain and opens the c-file a little.

moves.title: Black develops flexibly
moves.explanation: Ne7 supports c6/f5 and avoids blocking the c-pawn structure.

hints: Follow the highlighted move and say the idea out loud.
After each move, check king safety, center control, and piece activity.
When a trade appears, ask what file opens and which piece improves next.
coachingNotes: Black avoided the Italian with 1...e6, so this is a French Defense response branch.
The beginner plan is d4, e5, c3, develop, and understand the pawn chain.
Your chain points toward the kingside, but castle and develop before attacking.
Black will attack d4 with c5 and pieces. Defend the base of your chain calmly.

branches.title: If Black Plays d5: Scandinavian Response
branches.description: Black attacks e4 immediately. Capture, develop with tempo, and avoid chasing too far.

moves.title: Start with e4
moves.explanation: White claims the center and opens lines.

moves.title: Black chooses the Scandinavian
moves.explanation: d5 immediately attacks e4. This is not an Italian Game structure.

moves.title: Capture the pawn
moves.explanation: exd5 accepts the challenge and opens the e-file.

moves.title: Black recaptures with the queen
moves.explanation: Qxd5 brings the queen out early. White should gain time by developing.

moves.title: Develop with tempo
moves.explanation: Nc3 attacks the queen while developing a piece. This is exactly how to punish an early queen move.

moves.title: Black retreats the queen
moves.explanation: Qa5 keeps pressure while stepping away from the knight.

moves.title: Build the center
moves.explanation: d4 takes central space while Black's queen is already committed.

moves.title: Black develops
moves.explanation: Nf6 attacks the center and prepares castling.

moves.title: Develop normally
moves.explanation: Nf3 supports d4/e5 and helps White castle.

moves.title: Black gives the queen support
moves.explanation: c6 creates a safe square and supports central play.

moves.title: Develop the bishop
moves.explanation: Bc4 develops actively and points toward f7, now in an open-center game.

moves.title: Black develops the bishop
moves.explanation: Bf5 activates a piece before e6.

moves.title: Castle
moves.explanation: White has used development to gain time and now gets the king safe.

moves.title: Black solidifies
moves.explanation: e6 supports the center and opens the dark-square bishop.

hints: Follow the highlighted move and say the idea out loud.
After each move, check king safety, center control, and piece activity.
When a trade appears, ask what file opens and which piece improves next.
coachingNotes: Black avoided the Italian with 1...d5, so this is a Scandinavian response branch.
The beginner plan is simple: capture, develop with tempo on the queen, build the center, castle.
Do not chase the queen forever. Take the free development, then play normal chess.
After castling, look for active piece squares and central control rather than a premature attack.

ideas: The Italian Game starts only after e4 e5, Nf3 Nc6, and Bc4.
If Black plays c5, c6, e6, or d5 on move one, switch to the correct response instead of forcing Italian ideas.
In the quiet Italian, build with c3 and d3, castle, then prepare Re1 and a later d4 break.
Against other defenses, keep the same beginner values: center, development, king safety, then a clear plan.
Do not use f7 pressure or Bc4 ideas automatically when the pawn structure belongs to another opening.
commonMistakes: Trying to force the Italian after Black has already chosen the Sicilian, Caro-Kann, French, or Scandinavian.
Launching an f7 attack before castling or finishing development.
Playing random quiet moves instead of responding to the actual pawn structure.
Chasing the queen too far in the Scandinavian instead of taking development and castling.
Forgetting that each defense has its own central pawn breaks.
